methodology: AST-grep + regex grep across 28 TypeScript files; dependency analysis from package.json

files.usage: Synchronous file reading for email template loading at construction time
files.rationale: Template loading requires runtime filesystem access. Replace with preloaded templates or R2/KV fetch in Worker path. Not needed in Worker bundle — use Durable Objects or separate email service.
files.workerAlternative: Pre-render templates at build time, store in KV. Or delegate to external email microservice.

files.import: import { readFile, writeFile, ensureDir, remove, readdir, stat } from "fs-extra"
files.usage: Full filesystem operations for attachment CRUD
files.rationale: This is the FS-based attachment storage backend. The Worker equivalent is Cloudflare R2 for blob storage.
files.workerAlternative: R2 storage backend (already exists as S3AttachmentStorage pattern — swap S3Client for R2 binding).

files.usage: Reading TLS CA certificate file contents
files.rationale: TLS CA file reading can be replaced with inline cert string from env binding.
files.workerAlternative: Read from env.TLS_CA_FILE_CONTENTS or store in KV. D1 doesn't need TLS CA since it's internal.

files.usage: Dev migration tool — reads config files
files.rationale: Dev-only one-shot migration tool. Never belongs in Worker bundle.
files.workerAlternative: None needed — dev tool only.

files.usage: Path construction for file-based attachment storage
files.rationale: Used alongside fs operations. When FSAttachmentStorage is replaced with R2, path.join is no longer needed.
files.workerAlternative: String template literals `${vault}/${id}` for R2 object keys.

files.usage: Resolving .env file path from CLI args
files.rationale: Config loading is init-time only. Workers use env bindings — no path resolution needed.
files.workerAlternative: Workers receive config via env bindings — no file resolution.

files.usage: Resolving TLS CA file path
files.rationale: Same as fs usage — TLS CA resolution becomes env binding in Worker.
files.workerAlternative: Env binding or inline string.

files.usage: Resolving TLS CA file path for MongoDB connection
files.rationale: MongoDB storage backend itself is not Worker-compatible. Path usage goes with it.
files.workerAlternative: None — entire MongoDB storage backend is keep-outside.

files.usage: Resolving root directory and assets directory paths
files.rationale: Init-time path resolution for server bootstrap. Workers don't have cwd() or file system.
files.workerAlternative: Workers use env bindings and pre-configured values.

files.usage: Dev migration tool config path resolution
files.rationale: Dev tool — never in Worker bundle.
files.workerAlternative: None needed.

files.usage: Template directory path resolution
files.rationale: Part of email/SMTP subsystem that stays outside Worker.
files.workerAlternative: None — SMTP sender is keep-outside.

files.usage: Primary HTTP server for receiving requests
files.rationale: Core transport layer. Workers use fetch handler instead of http.createServer.
files.workerAlternative: export default { async fetch(request, env, ctx) }

files.usage: Outbound HTTP requests from HTTPSender
files.rationale: Outbound requests use global fetch() in Workers.
files.workerAlternative: global fetch() function.

files.usage: Legacy server HTTP client for migration compatibility
files.rationale: Legacy migration feature — not core Worker functionality.
files.workerAlternative: fetch() if needed, but legacy migration should remain a separate service.

files.usage: Standalone SCIM server listening on separate port (5000)
files.rationale: SCIM runs as independent HTTP server on its own port. Not composable into Worker fetch handler.
files.workerAlternative: Could be rewritten as a separate Cloudflare Worker route, but SCIM's complex stateful handling makes it better as a separate service.

files.usage: Stripe portal server listening on separate port (4000)
files.rationale: Stripe billing portal runs as independent HTTP micro-server. Not part of main request pipeline.
files.workerAlternative: Separate Cloudflare Worker for billing portal, or redirect to Stripe-hosted billing portal.

files.usage: API provisioner server on separate port (4000)
files.rationale: Provisioning API runs as independent server. Could potentially be merged into main Worker routes.
files.workerAlternative: Merged into main Worker fetch handler routes OR separate Worker.

files.usage: Outbound HTTPS requests from HTTPSender
files.rationale: Same as http — Workers use global fetch() for all outbound requests.
files.workerAlternative: global fetch() handles both HTTP and HTTPS.

files.usage: Legacy server HTTPS client
files.rationale: Part of legacy migration subsystem.
files.workerAlternative: fetch() if needed, but legacy stays outside Worker.

files.usage: Converting S3 response body stream to Uint8Array via Buffer.concat
files.rationale: S3 GetObject returns a Node Readable stream. In Workers, response.body is a Web ReadableStream of Uint8Array.
files.workerAlternative: response.arrayBuffer() or new Uint8Array(await response.arrayBuffer()) for R2 blob reads.

files.import: import { randomBytes, createHash, createHmac, sign, verify, constants, generateKeyPair, pbkdf2, createCipheriv, createDecipheriv, publicEncrypt, privateDecrypt, timingSafeEqual } from "crypto"
files.usage: Complete cryptographic provider — hashing, AES, RSA, HMAC, PBKDF2, signing
files.rationale: The entire crypto provider must be rewritten. Workers support Web Crypto API (crypto.subtle) with equivalent operations: SHA-256/512, AES-GCM, RSA-OAEP, HMAC, PBKDF2, ECDH.
files.workerAlternative: crypto.subtle: digest(), importKey(), sign(), verify(), encrypt(), decrypt(), deriveBits(). Note: Web Crypto uses Async-only API, unlike Node's sync+async mix.

files.usage: Buffer.concat() on stream chunks
files.rationale: Used with Node Readable stream. Web streams produce Uint8Array natively.
files.workerAlternative: native Uint8Array from Web ReadableStream chunks.

files.usage: Buffer[] array for request body accumulation, Buffer.concat(), Buffer.byteLength()
files.rationale: IncomingMessage chunks in Node are Buffer. Workers request.body is a Web ReadableStream.
files.workerAlternative: await request.arrayBuffer() or await request.text() — native Web APIs.

files.usage: Buffer.from() for encoding key material, Buffer.concat() for cipher output
files.rationale: Web Crypto API uses ArrayBuffer/Uint8Array directly — no Buffer needed.
files.workerAlternative: Uint8Array.from(), new Uint8Array(arrayBuffer), direct ArrayBuffer usage.

files.usage: URL parameter signing and verification for portal URLs
files.rationale: URLSearchParams is available as a global in Workers (Web API).
files.workerAlternative: Global URLSearchParams class — no import needed.

files.import: // import repl from "repl"; // import net from "net";
files.usage: REPL server for interactive console — all commented out
files.rationale: Fully commented out. Dev/ops tool only.
files.workerAlternative: None needed.

files.usage: REPL client entry point — commented out
files.rationale: Entire file is commented out.
files.workerAlternative: None needed.

files.usage: process.argv for --env flags, process.env for config, process.cwd()
files.rationale: Config bootstrapping — Workers use env bindings from wrangler.toml.
files.workerAlternative: env object passed to fetch handler. No process.argv or process.cwd().

files.usage: process.env.PL_ASSETS_DIR, process.env.PL_LEGACY_URL, process.env.PL_LEGACY_KEY, process.argv.includes('--dryrun'), process.exit(), process.on('uncaughtException')
files.rationale: Server lifecycle management — Workers don't have process events or explicit exit calls.
files.workerAlternative: env bindings for config. No uncaughtException handling — Worker handles errors per-request. No process.exit.

files.usage: process.cwd() for resolving TLS CA file path
files.rationale: Workers have no working directory concept.
files.workerAlternative: Env binding with full path or inline content.

files.usage: process.cwd() for TLS CA file resolution
files.rationale: MongoDB backend stays outside Worker entirely.
files.workerAlternative: None — whole backend is keep-outside.

files.usage: LevelDB key-value storage backend — the DEFAULT data storage
files.rationale: LevelDB is a native Node.js database. Workers use D1 (SQLite) or KV for equivalent functionality.
files.workerAlternative: Cloudflare D1 for structured data, KV for simple key-value. D1 is preferred since the storage API expects complex queries.

files.usage: PostgreSQL connection pool — alternative data storage backend
files.rationale: pg package uses Node.js net sockets. Workers cannot open raw TCP connections.
files.workerAlternative: Cloudflare D1 (SQLite via Hyperdrive) is the Worker-native relational DB. Migration SQL needed for PostgreSQL->D1 schema conversion.

files.usage: Dev migration tool — writes to PostgreSQL
files.rationale: Dev-only migration tool.
files.workerAlternative: None needed.

files.import: import { MongoClient, Db, Collection, ObjectId, Filter, FindOptions } from "mongodb"
files.usage: MongoDB connection and operations — alternative data storage backend
files.rationale: MongoDB driver requires TCP connections. Workers cannot connect to MongoDB directly.
files.workerAlternative: Cloudflare D1. Or keep MongoDB but access via a separate Node.js microservice proxied through Workers.

files.usage: ObjectId usage for MongoDB log storage
files.rationale: Follows MongoDBStorage — stays outside Worker if MongoDB is externalized.
files.workerAlternative: None — MongoDB logging stays outside.

files.usage: Dev migration tool — reads from MongoDB
files.rationale: Dev tool only.
files.workerAlternative: None needed.

files.usage: SMTP email delivery
files.rationale: nodemailer uses TCP sockets for SMTP. Workers cannot make raw TCP connections. Email sending should be delegated to a separate Node.js service or use an API-based email provider.
files.workerAlternative: Email API service (Resend, SendGrid, SES) called via HTTP fetch from Worker. Or delegate to separate email microservice.

files.import: import { DeleteObjectCommand, GetObjectCommand, PutObjectCommand, ListObjectsCommand, DeleteObjectsCommand, S3Client } from "@aws-sdk/client-s3"
files.usage: S3-based attachment storage
files.rationale: @aws-sdk/client-s3 can work in Workers with nodejs_compat but is heavy. Cloudflare R2 is the native equivalent with S3-compatible API and zero egress fees.
files.workerAlternative: Cloudflare R2 binding — env.R2_BUCKET.get/put/delete/list. S3-compatible API makes migration straightforward.

files.usage: Downloads MaxMind GeoLite2 database files from filesystem
files.rationale: Downloads and opens .dat database files using Node fs. Workers cannot write to or read from filesystem.
files.workerAlternative: Cloudflare's built-in geolocation is available via request.cf.country, request.cf.city, request.cf.region. No external database needed.

files.usage: Opens and queries MaxMind database files for IP -> location lookup
files.rationale: Requires loading database files into memory. Replaced by Cloudflare's native geolocation.
files.workerAlternative: request.cf object provides country, city, region, latitude, longitude natively.

files.usage: Creates DOMParser environment for DOMPurify HTML sanitization
files.rationale: JSDOM emulates a full DOM environment — very heavy and unnecessary in Workers which have native DOMParser.
files.workerAlternative: Workers have native DOMParser API. Initialize DOMPurify with DOMPurify(new DOMParser()) or use native DOMParser directly.

files.usage: HTML sanitization for email template interpolation
files.rationale: DOMPurify requires a DOM environment. Workers can use DOMParser-based sanitization or trusted-types approach.
files.workerAlternative: Native DOMParser with sanitization, or use a lighter library like 'sanitize-html' that doesn't need a DOM.

files.usage: Loading .env file for development configuration
files.rationale: Workers use wrangler.toml env and secret bindings — no .env file loading.
files.workerAlternative: wrangler.toml [vars] and wrangler secret put.

files.usage: Stripe SDK for billing, subscriptions, and checkout sessions
files.rationale: Stripe SDK uses Node.js HTTP module and is designed for server-side. Can work in Workers with compatibility mode, but billing is better handled as a separate service.
files.workerAlternative: Stripe REST API via fetch() calls from Worker. Or keep as separate Node.js billing microservice called from Worker via HTTP.

files.usage: Mixpanel analytics event logging
files.rationale: Mixpanel SDK uses Node http module. Workers can send events via fetch() to Mixpanel's HTTP API directly.
files.workerAlternative: Direct fetch() to Mixpanel API endpoint: https://api.mixpanel.com/track

files.usage: WebAuthn authentication — credential verification and generation
files.rationale: @simplewebauthn/server depends on Node.js crypto module for CBOR decoding of credential public keys and signature verification. Not directly compatible with Workers.
files.workerAlternative: Manual WebAuthn verification using crypto.subtle and CBOR parsing, or use a Workers-compatible WebAuthn library.

files.usage: Buffer.from(base64ToBytes(...)) for WebAuthn credential ID and public key conversion
files.rationale: Buffer usage for data conversion. Works with Uint8Array directly.
files.workerAlternative: Uint8Array.from() or direct Uint8Array usage.

criticalPath: crypto/node.ts — must rewrite entire crypto provider to crypto.subtle (blocks ALL auth, encryption, signing)
transport/http.ts — must replace http.createServer with Worker fetch handler (blocks request handling)
storage/leveldb.ts — default storage backend must become D1 or KV
storage/postgres.ts — pg Pool must become D1 Hyperdrive
attachments/s3.ts — S3 stream/Buffer must become R2 binding
attachments/fs.ts — fs-extra must become R2 binding
init.ts — entire server bootstrap must be restructured for Worker lifecycle

notes: No `node:` prefix imports found — all use bare module names.
@padloc/core dependency was NOT analyzed for Node imports — this task scoped to packages/server/src only.
The repl.ts and init-repl-client.ts files are fully commented out and classified as delete.
tools/mongo2postgres.ts is a one-shot migration tool classified as delete.
Worker-native alternatives leverage: crypto.subtle, fetch(), D1, KV, R2, Cloudflare geolocation (request.cf).
nodejs_compat is NOT considered a resolution per task requirements.
Some keep-outside services (Stripe, SMTP, SCIM) should become separate Workers or external microservices.
